general_information.Description: Inside Reading 4 combines reading skills development with key vocabulary from the Academic Word List, to give students the tools they need to understand academic texts. Each unit features two high interest readings. Topics include Sociology, Nutrition, Architecture, and Business, among many others. At the higher levels of Inside Reading, reading texts are adapted from authentic, well-known sources such as the Wall Street Journal, Popular Science, and The New York Times, and from acclaimed authors such as Malcolm Gladwell, James Surowiecki, and Jared Diamond. Authentic readings expose students to real-world, high interest content and authentic language. Explicit reading skill instruction provides the foundation for effective critical reading. At all levels, Inside Reading covers reading skills that are vital to student success in the academic classroom, such as previewing and predicting, finding the main idea, scanning, and evaluating.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Attend more than 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose - Read the textbook in advance - Access the course website (www.cms.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Skim and scan the text for information; outline the information while reading
Find the main ideas, isolate causes and effects
Find the perpetrator and identify different point of view
Catergorize information, interprete charts, tables and graphs
Describe trends, summarize and report the information
Analyze advantages and disadvantages, identify ethics and values
Identify multiple causes, synthesize information from several sources

assessments.Question Type: 1. A report to describe and summarize information using data given in graphs/ diagram / tables; 2. An essay to present opinions, arguments, solutions
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Students write to complete two essays using the techniques learnt in the respective units. Focus of each test is described in the detailed contents in Appendix 1
assessments.Grading Guide: In classroom, supervised by class instructor/s
assessments.Note: The tests must be designed based on the skills covered in the tested units.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Students write to complete two essays using the techniques learnt in 10 units
assessments.Note: Do not allow to use any document/information in any form in exam room
